content.title: About
content.content: A quesadilla is a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a thin corn or wheat tortilla filled with melted cheese and often complemented by meat, vegetables, beans, or sauces. The NFS (New Flavor Series) version uses a special cheese blend that gives a brighter taste and aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Quesadillas originated in Mexico during pre‑Columbian times, originally using corn masa flatbreads.
The word “quesadilla” derives from the Spanish “queso” – cheese.
In the United States, quesadillas gained popularity in the 1990s through fast‑casual Mexican chains.
The NFS variant features a proprietary cheese sauce developed with executive chefs.
Traditionally, quesadillas are cooked on an open flame or a dry skillet without oil.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Cheese and meat or bean fillings provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Cheese is an excellent source of calcium, supporting bone and dental health.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Both the tortilla and cheese supply B1, B2, and B12 vitamins that aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Meat and bean additions deliver iron, crucial for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Satiety support
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps maintain a feeling of fullness longer.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Quesadillas, especially those with meat fillings, can be calorie‑dense, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Cheese and sauces often contain significant salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten in wheat tortilla
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should opt for corn tortillas.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the quesadilla on a dry skillet, in the oven, or in a microwave until the tortilla is golden and the cheese melts. Cut into triangles and serve with salsa, guacamole, sour cream, or fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked quesadillas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Freeze in a separate bag at –18 °C, then reheat thoroughly before serving.
